chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan from Ibn Muskan from Waleed the seller of carpets, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, while I was in his presence, about a girl who had two brothers: the elder married her in Kufa, and the younger married her in another land. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The first is more entitled to her, unless the other has already consummated the marriage with her. If he has consummated it with her, then she is his wife and his marriage is valid.'
ai.seo_question: Who has the right to marry a sister if two brothers marry her to different men?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) clarifies the hierarchy of *wilayah al-nikah* among co-guardians, establishing that the elder brother holds primary authority unless the younger brother has already consummated the marriage, in which case his union is deemed valid and exclusive. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential balance between hierarchical seniority and the sanctity of consummation (*dakhala*), ensuring legal certainty in cases of concurrent marriages. The narration underscores the practical application of guardianship rights within the extended family structure, a key topic in *fiqh al-nikah*.
